title: On three open problems in zero-sum Ramsey numbers
summary: Let $K_N^{(r)}$ denote the $N$-vertex complete $r$-uniform hypergraph. For an $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ and an integer $k\geq2$, the $k$-color Ramsey number $R(H,k)$ is the least integer $N$ such that every $k$-edge-coloring of $K_N^{(r)}$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$. When $k\mid\esize(H)$, the zero-sum Ramsey number $R(H,\mathbb Z_k)$ is the least integer $N$ such that every edge-labeling of $K_N^{(r)}$ by elements of $\mathbb Z_k$ contains a copy of $H$ whose edge labels sum to $0$ in $\mathbb Z_k$. We settle two conjectures and a problem concerning these two Ramsey numbers.…
